title: Optional-output reader soundness
statement: For every bit string $x$, optional bit $b$, and bit string $r$, if the optional-output reader succeeds on $x$ with result $(b,r)$, then $x$ is the two-bit code for $b$—$00$ for no output, $10$ for output $0$, or $11$ for output $1$—followed by $r$.
hypotheses_covered: the optional-output reader succeeds on $x$ with result $(b,r)$
replaced:
If the optional-output reader succeeds on a bit string $x$, returning a value
$b$ and a suffix $r$, then $x$ is exactly the two-bit dictionary code of $b$
followed by $r$.
